items.title: A dip in gold prices brings out jewelry shoppers in Mississauga on Diwali weekend
items.summary: As gold prices dip, some shoppers are taking advantage by buying jewelry during the South Asian festival of Diwali.

items.title: Scandinavian discount store set to open at Square One in Mississauga
items.summary: A Danish variety store known for quirky, low-cost products is coming to Mississauga just in time for holiday shopping. Flying Tiger Copenhagen is set to open its new store at Square One Shopping Centre on Saturday, Nov. 14, with a location at CF Markville in Markham opening two days earlier, on Thursday, Nov. 12. The retailer sells home decor, stationery, toys, kitchenware, party supplies and seasonal items. According to the company, more than 80 per cent of its products are priced under $10, and about 27 per cent are under $5. Around 300 new items arrive in stores each month. The chain was founded in Copenhagen in 1995, originally under the name Tiger, and now operates more than 1,000 stores in 45 markets. Canada became its 45th market this year. Its first Canadian store opened at CF Toronto Eaton Centre in June. In announcing its arrival in Canada, the company said the GTA was the first step in a broader rollout across the Americas. Locations at Vaughan Mills and Scarborough Town Centre are also part of its GTA plans. “We see strong alignment with Canadian consumers who appreciate design-led products at accessible prices,” Jens Aarup Mikkelsen, CEO of Flying Tiger Copenhagen, said in the release. The stores are designed to be walked through like a maze, so shoppers pass all 14 product categories.

items.title: Dixie Road Tops List as Nearly 300 Vehicles Stolen Across Mississauga and Brampton in a Month
items.summary: Peel Regional Police data shows thieves stole 283 vehicles across Mississauga and Brampton between Oct. 7 and Nov. 7, averaging about nine thefts a day. According to insauga.com, Mississauga accounted for 167 of those thefts while Brampton saw 116. The outlet reported that cars made up the bulk of the stolen vehicles, with 201 automobiles taken alongside 60 trucks, 17 motorcycles and five vehicles in other categories. In Mississauga, Dixie Road saw the most thefts with 10 reported, followed by nine on Airport Road, five on Argentia Road, four on Britannia Road and three in the City Centre area. Brampton's hot spots included seven thefts on Great Lakes Drive and four each on Bramtree Court and Coventry Road, insauga.com said. Peel police are asking anyone with information to call 905-453-3311 or contact Peel Crime Stoppers anonymously at 1-800-222-TIPS.

items.title: Legal Experts Say Law Is Unclear on Filming Police During Live Operations
items.summary: A tense standoff with an armed suspect at the University of Toronto's Mississauga campus has sparked a debate over whether it's appropriate to livestream police movements during an active incident. According to CBC Toronto, officers responding to the Monday night standoff issued a stern warning after social media users posted real-time footage showing police positions on the scene. The broadcaster reported that legal experts say Canadian law offers no clear-cut answer on whether filming and sharing an active police operation crosses a line, since it sits at the intersection of free expression and officer safety. CBC Toronto said police have long worried that revealing tactical positions in real time could tip off a suspect and put officers and bystanders at risk. The debate echoes similar controversies in other cities, where livestreamed footage of active incidents has drawn scrutiny from both civil liberties advocates and law enforcement. CBC Toronto noted the broader legal question remains unresolved.

items.title: Mississauga's Laeticia Amihere Becomes Second Canadian Ever to Win a WNBA Title
items.summary: Laeticia Amihere, a 25-year-old forward from Mississauga, became just the second Canadian ever to win a WNBA championship after her Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the Finals. According to the Toronto Star, Amihere was introduced as the team's enforcer at a victory parade Wednesday that drew an estimated 400,000 fans to the San Francisco Bay Area, and told the paper the nickname fits since she has always been known for her tenacity. The Star reported Amihere previously won gold with Canada's under-16 team at the 2015 FIBA Americas championship, took third at the 2017 under-19 World Cup and won an NCAA title with the South Carolina Gamecocks in 2022. She did not see the court in Game 7 but had 10 rebounds in 20 minutes in Game 6, contributing to a Valkyries team that won it all in just its second season. The only other Canadian to win a WNBA championship is Markham's Tammy Sutton-Brown, who did so with the Indiana Fever in 2012, the paper said. Amihere is set to travel to Senegal next week to continue work with her sports non-profit, Back to the Motherland.

items.title: Mississauga's Goat-Grazing Program to Continue Through 2027 After Early Success
items.summary: The City of Mississauga plans to keep using herds of grazing goats to fight invasive plant species through 2027 and beyond, after three years of what officials call a groundbreaking success. According to insauga.com, the city has brought in the goats each spring through early fall since 2024, using the animals as natural lawnmowers to control non-native species like buckthorn, phragmites and reed canary grass in meadows and prairies. Mississauga was the first municipality in Ontario to use goat grazing for invasive species control when it launched the program, the outlet reported. City spokesperson Irene McCutcheon told insauga.com the grazing has reduced the extent, density and size of invasive plant populations at treated sites, with the strongest results coming at sites that have been grazed repeatedly. McCutcheon said those sites have generally needed little to no follow-up manual control. Beyond the environmental results, she said the goats have also become ambassadors for the city's invasive species and pest management program through events like the annual Invasive Species Awareness Fair.

items.title: Clearance Warehouse Opens Oakville Location Just West of the Mississauga Border
items.summary: A new discount retailer has opened just outside Mississauga, giving bargain hunters another option for deals on household goods and name-brand merchandise. According to insauga.com, Clearance Warehouse opened its newest location on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 2307 Royal Windsor Drive in Oakville, in a roughly 30,000-square-foot space that previously housed a RONA store just west of the Mississauga border. The store is stocked with liquidation, overstock and clearance merchandise advertised at discounts of 30 to 90 per cent off regular retail prices, including housewares, small appliances, bedding, health and beauty products and tools. The selection is expected to change regularly as new stock arrives and existing inventory sells through. The Oakville store joins existing Clearance Warehouse locations in Brampton and Etobicoke, both of which opened for the current sale period in October, with all three locations running their sales until Dec. 24.

items.title: Local History Group Traces Mississauga's Military Service Back to the War of 1812
items.summary: Modern Mississauga Media is marking Remembrance Day this year by tracing the city's long history of military service, stretching back well before Mississauga's own borders existed. According to the outlet, some of the area's earliest settlers were veterans of the American Revolution who arrived as Loyalists, and residents of historic Toronto Township later volunteered for militia service along the Niagara frontier during the War of 1812, alongside Indigenous Mississaugas from the Credit River. The outlet reported that although no conflict ever reached Mississauga itself, residents went on to serve in the Rebellion of 1837, the Fenian Raids, both World Wars, the Korean War, the Gulf War, Kosovo, Afghanistan and numerous peacekeeping missions. During the First World War, hundreds of local men enlisted with the Canadian Expeditionary Force and 96 soldiers from historic Mississauga died in service, the outlet said. It also noted that historic Mississauga was home to the Long Branch Aerodrome, Canada's first military flight school, which produced 129 graduates who went on to serve with the Royal Air Force and Royal Naval Air Service in Britain.

items.title: Mississauga Targets 4,100-Tonne Cut to Winter Road Salt Use
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says it plans to significantly reduce how much road salt it uses this winter, aiming to protect the environment and infrastructure while keeping roads safe for drivers. According to city officials, the expanded salt-reduction effort is expected to cut road salt use by as much as 4,100 tonnes a year. The city said it will extend anti-icing brine, a liquid mix of water and salt, to 20 per cent more roads in 2026, a change expected to reduce salt use by up to 650 tonnes annually. Officials said they will also begin plowing snow earlier on select major roads, a step they estimate could cut salt use by a further 3,450 tonnes a year. The brine program currently covers about 1,260 lane kilometres of roadway, using roughly 63,000 litres of salt brine for each application, city officials said.

items.title: Food Basics to Replace Decades-Old Metro Store at Lakeshore Plaza
items.summary: A Mississauga grocery store with a history stretching back decades has closed, according to insauga.com, marking the end of an era for a Lakeview neighbourhood shopping plaza. The Metro location at 406 Lakeshore Road East, in the Lakeshore Plaza near Cawthra Road, shut its doors on Nov. 4 after operating over the years under several different banners, including Miracle Food Mart and Dominion before becoming Metro. The site reported the space is being converted into a Food Basics store, with the discount grocery banner expected to open sometime in the new year. The parent company has been converting a number of its traditional Metro locations into Food Basics stores as shoppers increasingly look for ways to save on groceries, insauga.com said. The Lakeshore Plaza location will remain under the same corporate ownership even as its shopping format changes.
